children.why_this_cut: The risky situations section opening plus the imminent-harm and illicit-behavior subsections; the only crossing linkage is the risky_situations section concept, seeded below.
The self-harm, regulated-advice, and mental-health subsections; the only crossing linkage is the risky_situations section concept, seeded below.

seed_vocabulary.name: risky_situations
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section providing instructions for handling requests that involve risky situations (imminent harm, illicit behavior, self-harm, regulated advice, mental health)

seed_vocabulary.name: prevent_imminent_harm
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule that the assistant should proactively try to prevent imminent real-world harm and avoid advice that could result in immediate physical harm

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule that the assistant should refuse to help facilitate or encourage illicit behavior

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_encourage_self_harm
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule that the assistant must not encourage or enable self-harm and should respond supportively to credible risk

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_regulated_advice
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule that the assistant should provide information without giving definitive regulated advice (legal, medical, financial) and include a disclaimer

seed_vocabulary.name: support_mental_health
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule that the assistant should create a supportive, empathetic environment in mental health discussions and avoid judgment or harmful behavior

seed_vocabulary.name: protect_privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should avoid sharing private or privileged data, or enabling new access to such data, without explicit authorization

judgment_calls: Chose three children rather than two: the privileged-information section (L1798-1973) is a distinct topic from the risky-situations subsections, and the self-harm/regulated-advice/mental-health block (L1543-1797) is cohesive enough to stand alone. A two-way split would have forced a cut inside the mental-health subsection or merged two unrelated sections.
The risky_situations seed is inherited from the parent dispatch and carried unchanged; it is established at the section heading L1414 and spans the whole section through L1755.

The prevent_imminent_harm, do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior, do_not_encourage_self_harm, avoid_regulated_advice, support_mental_health, and protect_privileged_information seeds are newly coined here because they are established in one child and used in another; they are the naming authority for these cross-cutting concepts.
